text.p: Incomnet Inc said Thursday it has settled two lawsuits involving current and former shareholder plaintiffs for $800,000.

Incomnet said in a statement it agreed to pay $400,000 in cash and a note for $400,000 plus interest, due and payable in one year and collateralized by a certificate of deposit. The lawsuits against Incomnet were dismissed with prejudice.

Melvyn Reznick, chairman and chief executive officer of Incomnet, said the company believed the plaintiffs claims were without merit, but Incomnet decided to settle to avoid the costs and risks of litigation and to allow management to focus on developing the company's operations.

The lawsuits are Herbert Schwartz et al vs Incomnet, Sam Schwartz and Kaliber Management Corp and Brent Abrahm et al vs Incomnet, Sam Schwartz and Kaliber Management, pending before the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California in Los Angeles. Herbert Schwartz, one of the lead plaintiffs, and Sam Schwartz, the company's former president and chief executive officer, are not related.
